title: ModelCitizens: Representing Community Voices in Online Safety
findings: The study found significant variations in toxicity perception for content targeting religious groups. For posts targeting Jewish and Muslim communities, 'amplified harm' (where outgroup annotators perceive harm that ingroup members do not) was more prevalent than 'missed harm'. Adding conversational context often changed toxicity labels, notably reclassifying previously toxic-rated posts targeting Muslims as non-toxic. Model performance varied by group; for example, LLAMACITIZEN-8B had its lowest performance on content targeting Jewish people, highlighting the difficulty in detecting toxicity for this group. Conversely, GPT-4o and Gemini-2.0-Flash had the highest performance for content targeting Muslims among the baseline models.
